nodes.description: Pan-neural knockdown of Drosophila Prp19 changes exon usage in several hundred genes in larval brain, including increased inclusion of exons in Iswi, Brm, RpS19a and Rbfox1, rather than abolishing splicing. The evidence is from ortholog knockdown only; no splicing assay of a patient PRPF19 variant or of patient-derived cells has been reported, and restoring Iswi or Rbfox1 did not rescue the Prp19 knockdown brain phenotype, so the disease-relevant splicing targets are unknown. Knockdown models loss of function, while most patient variants are WD40 missense changes whose effect on PRPF19 dosage or activity is not known.

nodes.description: Pan-neural knockdown of the fly PRPF19 ortholog with two independent RNAi lines, and rescue by wild-type or patient-variant human PRPF19.

A heterozygous de novo PRPF19 variant alters PRPF19, the U-box E3 ubiquitin ligase that forms the core of the Prp19 (NTC) complex with CDC5L and BCAS2 and assembles the other NTC-associated proteins through its C-terminal WD40 domain. Missense variants cluster in the WD40 beta-propeller and are predicted from structural modelling to destabilize propeller folding; the frameshift p.(His273Thrfs*37) truncates the WD40 domain. The ubiquitin ligase activity is bound here as the protein's own molecular function; no study has measured the effect of a patient variant on it.

nodes.description: A de novo 400 kb duplication spanning PRPF19 increases gene dosage. In the fly, overexpression of wild-type human PRPF19 increases brain cell proliferation, which the authors relate to the macrocephaly and tall stature of the individual carrying the duplication. The duplication spans other genes, so attribution of the phenotype to PRPF19 is not certain. This node is not declared conformant to the spliceosome module's variant node, which describes reduced dosage or altered sequence.

nodes.description: Pan-neural knockdown of fly Prp19 reduces larval brain cell proliferation, shrinks both lobes of the mushroom body, causes larval hypoactivity and is lethal before eclosion. Wild-type human PRPF19 and the two tested missense variants rescue lethality and the mushroom body defect, with p.(Gly404Ser) rescuing proliferation less completely, while the truncated p.(His273Thrfs*37) protein rescues neither. Both missense variants fail to restore normal social spacing in adult flies.
